page: Microsoft Azure E128-64ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V and powered by an x86_64 Intel processor platform. This configuration operates as a constrained-core variant within the Edsv6 family, exposing 64 dedicated vCPUs from a larger 128-core physical footprint. It provides 1024.0 GB of system memory, achieving an extensive memory-to-core allocation of 16.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware setup does not include discrete GPU acceleration.

Storage infrastructure on this instance features 7560 GB of attached local NVMe SSD storage designed for fast temporary scratch space, swap files, and high-throughput paging. Additionally, the instance is equipped for Premium Storage integration to accommodate persistent cloud disk attachments. Network allocations do not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating standard Azure virtual networking components for external ingress and egress routing.

The constrained 64-vCPU topology provides distinct qualitative cost efficiencies for software suites licensed on a per-core basis, such as commercial relational database management systems. Organizations requiring a full terabyte of RAM and extensive low-latency local NVMe capacity can run heavy data operations without incurring the licensing overhead of a full 128-core deployment. Typical workload fits for this server include enterprise in-memory databases, large Redis or Memcached clusters, heavy transactional databases, real-time analytics engines, and data transformation pipelines.
